title.narrative: Food security and livelihood support for IDPs and vulnerable communities in Shekan

description.narrative: In 2015, the locality of Shikan was severely impacted by El Niño which delayed and reduced rainfall which in turn hampered agricultural activities. Delayed planting, poor pastures and limited water availability for both people and their livestock has been a major concern. Field reports (from SIDO field team) indicated that farmers have reduced cultivated areas in some parts and substituted cultivation of the millets e.g. by other cash crops (sesame), although millets is the main staple food in North Kordofan. Due to the poor harvest 2015 season and a lean season in March 2016 there has been increase of number of acute food insecure in people in North Kordofan. The proposed project seeks to address the challenges of food and income security for the poor and vulnerable households in the Skikan locality North Kordfan state, to build their capacity to adapt to the myriad of the DRR-related issues. The project targets 1275 HH (875 women and 400 men) Expected outputs include: 1.500 households in Shaken locality demonstrating improved food security through use of improved small scale agricultural techniques by July, 2017. 2. 5,000 animals belonging to 200 pastoralist, families in Algesip and Alhakona villages in Shekan locality have improved animal health condition by July 2017. 3. 20 household in HayAlarab village, Shekan locality have improved income through establishment of 30 saving and loans groups by July 2017. 4. By July 2017, 300 household in Um Habila, Elarab quarter and Um Heglig villages in Shikan locality have capacity to analyse, prepare and adapt to various climate/man-made related disasters.
